title: The Queen of Adjamé Market
author: Léxi
desc: Mama Adjoua vend des tomates au marché. Sa fille Esther veut tout changer avec un téléphone.

p: In Adjamé market, everybody knows Mama Adjoua. She sells tomatoes, onions and peppers under a big blue umbrella. She has a loud voice and a big laugh.
"Fresh tomatoes! Red like love! Come, my daughter, come, my son!" she calls all day.

Mama Adjoua starts work at four in the morning. She buys vegetables from the trucks that come from the north. Then she sells them, one by one, until the sun goes down. Her hands are strong. Her feet are tired. But she never complains.
Her daughter Esther is seventeen. Every day after school, Esther comes to help. She is good at mathematics, and she loves her phone.
"Mama, you work too hard," says Esther. "And you lose too many tomatoes. Look, half of these are going bad."
Mama Adjoua sighs. "Tomatoes don't wait, my child. If nobody buys them today, tomorrow they are rubbish."
One evening, Esther shows her mother a WhatsApp group on her phone.
"Mama, look. I made a group. 'Mama Adjoua's Fresh Vegetables.' I added our neighbours, my teachers, the women from church."
"And what is it for?"
"Every morning, I take a photo of your best vegetables. People order on the phone. Then I deliver after school on my bicycle."
Mama Adjoua laughs her big laugh. "Who buys tomatoes on a telephone?"
But the next morning, Esther posts a photo. Red tomatoes, green peppers, purple onions. By eight o'clock, there are twelve orders. By noon, there are twenty-five.
Mama Adjoua stops laughing. She puts on her glasses and looks at the phone.
"Twenty-five orders?" she whispers. "Before lunch?"
After one month, the group has three hundred people. Esther cannot deliver everything on her bicycle. She is tired. Her school results are going down.
One day, her teacher, Mr. Bamba, calls her.
"Esther, you were the best in maths. Now you sleep in class. What is happening?"
Esther tells him everything. The tomatoes. The group. The deliveries in the evening.
Mr. Bamba is quiet. Then he says: "Your idea is very good, Esther. But a good business needs a good team. You cannot do everything alone."
That night, Esther cannot sleep. She thinks about the word *team*.
In the morning, she has a new idea. In the market, there are many young boys with motorbikes who have no work. And there are many women like her mother who lose vegetables every day.
Esther talks to the other women in the market. Mama Fanta who sells fish. Mama Rose who sells bananas. Old Mama Akissi who sells spices.
"We can sell together," she explains. "One group, one market, on the phone. The boys deliver on their motorbikes. Everybody pays a small amount for the delivery."
At first, the women don't trust the idea. Phones are for young people, they say. But Mama Adjoua stands up.
"My daughter is right," she says with her loud voice. "Last month, I didn't lose one tomato. Not one!"
The women look at each other. Then Mama Fanta laughs. "If Mama Adjoua says it, it must be true!"

Three months later, the group "Adjamé Market at Home" has two thousand people. Ten boys deliver on motorbikes. The women lose almost nothing. And Esther only works one hour every evening, because the team does the rest.
At the end of the year, Esther gets the best maths result in her school. Mr. Bamba shakes her hand.
"What do you want to study now?" he asks.
"Business," says Esther. "I want to help all the markets in Côte d'Ivoire."
That evening, there is a small party under the big blue umbrella. The women bring food. The boys bring music. Mama Adjoua wears her most beautiful pagne.
She stands up and raises her glass of bissap.
"They call me the queen of Adjamé market," she says. "But tonight I want to say the truth. The real queen is my daughter."
Everybody claps. Esther's eyes fill with tears.
"No, Mama," she says. "I only had a phone. You had the courage to work every day for thirty years. You are the queen. I am just the princess."
And under the blue umbrella, everybody laughs, the big laugh of Mama Adjoua.
